key_insight: LLM2R reformulates 3D part assembly as a single-pass sequence modeling problem, using an adapted decoder-only LLM to predict all rigid part poses jointly with global context.
engineering_relevance: This improves scalable assembly of fractured or disassembled parts in robotics, digital reconstruction, and CAD pipelines, especially as part counts grow.
method: Encode each part with Point-BERT + Q-Former into geometric token blocks
Concatenate all part tokens and process them with a causal LLM adapted by LoRA
Add learnable summary tokens plus a part-aware pose head to predict SE(3) transforms for every part in one forward pass
evidence_signal: The method reports top performance across three PartNet categories, PartNeXt, and Breaking Bad, with particularly large gains at 100 parts and strong zero-shot transfer to unseen categories.
watch_item: Because causal attention limits each part to earlier parts, performance may depend on part ordering and careful tokenization/summary-token design.
paper_title: LLM2R: From Large Language Models to 3D Reassemblers
